pages.text: A simulated Kerr-Newman black hole: mass, spin and charge, nothing else (the no-hair theorem). Its horizons, temperature and innermost stable orbit follow exactly. Cosmic censorship forbids a²+Q² > M².
$(thing)Set$(): Spin a/M, Charge Q/M, Confinement field, Mass.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Frame-dragging noise: the effective spin is a + 0.002·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): a² + Q² > M²: naked singularity - cosmic censorship violated; Charge not held: field too weak; Interlock: charge-confinement coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the charge-confinement coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Simulations run at a fixed pace.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Censorship margin: 1 − a² − Q²$(br)Outer horizon r₊: r₊ = M + √(M² − a² − Q²)$(br)Inner horizon r₋: r₋ = M − √(M² − a² − Q²)$(br)Surface gravity κ: κ = (r₊ − r₋)/(2(r₊² + a²))$(br)Hawking temperature: T = ħκ/(2πk)$(br)Horizon angular velocity: Ω_H = a/(r₊² + a²)$(br)Innermost stable orbit: r_ISCO = 3 + Z₂ − √((3 − Z₁)(3 + Z₁ + 2Z₂))
